title: Cultivation transforms the Kuk wetlands
summary: At Kuk in the highlands of New Guinea, archaeological traces show the development of plant cultivation and wetland modification. UNESCO describes a transformation toward agriculture around 6,500 years ago.

claims.text: At Kuk in the highlands of New Guinea, archaeological traces show the development of plant cultivation and wetland modification. UNESCO describes a transformation toward agriculture around 6,500 years ago.
Approximate 6,500 years-ago statement; rounded 4,500 BCE anchor. Earlier wetland activity is distinct.
Drainage and cultivation offer evidence for a regional history of farming. This record is one comparison point, not a claim that all agriculture came from a single origin.
